title: Mitigate and Fix Hosted API 5xx/timeouts triggered by retry storms during escalations
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Summary: Multiple high-value customers reported repeated 5xx responses and long request timeouts against the Hosted API during a coordinated escalation window. Symptoms included 502/503 response bursts, client-observed timeouts >30s, and cascading retries from SDKs that amplified load, causing partial regional degradation. The issue has affected both Hosted and cross-routed Dedicated traffic due to routing fallback logic. This ticket tracks triage, short-term mitigations, the engineering fix, rollout, and postmortem items.
impact_examples:
- Customer: AcmeDocs (enterprise) saw 30% of requests return 502s for 12 minutes on 2026-02-19 15:34-15:46 UTC.
- Customer: QuickChat encountered repeated token-generation timeouts and invoked client retries, tripling upstream request rate.
- Platform telemetry: p50 latency increased to 1200ms and 5xx rate spiked to 4.2% in us-west-2 during the window.
timeline:
2026-02-19 15:32 UTC: Pager alert: hosted-api-5xx-rate > 1% on prod-us-west-2.
2026-02-19 15:34 UTC: Initial P1 zoom with oncall.
2026-02-19 15:40 UTC: Identified correlation with model-fallback routing events and increased retries from SDKs.
2026-02-19 15:45 UTC: Short mitigation applied: reduce default SDK retries to 1 for public SDKs and disabled auto-fallback to heavy compute variants.
2026-02-19 16:10 UTC: 5xx rate falling; mitigation left in place while engineering investigates root cause.
2026-02-20 to 2026-03-09: Deep investigation and multiple code reviews for routing/backpressure changes.
2026-03-10: This ticket created/updated to consolidate final rollout plan and acceptance criteria.
reproduction_steps:
1) Simulate sustained burst of requests with typical client-side retry policy (3 retries, exponential backoff) against model route that has a configured fallback to a dedicated heavy variant.
2) Induce backend slowdowns by adding artificial latency to one dedicated pool (use canary harness).
3) Observe Gateway/Router logs for retry amplification, queue growth, and 5xx responses.
4) Verify metrics: per-route concurrency, queue latency, 5xx rate, and KV-cache hit ratio.
investigation_notes:
- Root causes identified: (a) routing fallback policy lacks backpressure signaling; when primary model pool slows, Router rapidly retries to fallback pool, which had lower capacity, causing overload; (b) SDK default retries (3) and lack of jitter created synchronized retry storms; (c) health-check cadence for Dedicated pools was too slow to trigger earlier failover; (d) circuit-breaker thresholds in the gateway were overly permissive.
- Secondary finding: prefix KV caching was disabled for a subset of routes, increasing per-request work during the incident.
- Evidence: kinesis logs: https://logs.internal.redwood/acme/incident-20260219, dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/hosted-api/5xx-spike-us-west-2
short_term_mitigations:
(already applied)
- Reduce public SDK default retries from 3->1 and promote jitter in client libraries (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789).
- Disable auto-fallback to heavy dedicated variants as default during high-latency windows (feature flag set at 2026-02-19T15:45Z).
- Emergency per-customer rate limiting for affected tenants (AcmeDocs, QuickChat) until stable.
- Manually increase health-check frequency for dedicated pools to 5s for the affected region.
Remaining short-term actions:
- Add immediate alert for retry-amplification ratio > 1.5 to detect repeat patterns.
long_term_fixes:
- Implement backpressure propagation: router->upstream should include X-backpressure header and upstreams must honor priority/queue admission.
- Add per-route concurrency ceilings and queue-length caps with token-bucket admission to prevent head-of-line amplification.
- Harden routing fallback algorithm to use slow-start and capacity-weighted selection, not naive round-robin.
- Make health-checks adaptive: increase frequency when neighboring pools show elevated queue latency.
- Rework gateway circuit-breaker defaults and add an exponential cool-off policy to prevent thrashing.
- Ensure KV/prefix cache is enabled for all high-throughput routes by default.
- Add integration test harness that simulates SDK retry storms and validates backpressure behavior.
design_decisions:
- Chosen pattern: admission control + informative headers (backpressure) rather than global client-side retry limits because we want server-side protection even when clients are misconfigured.
- We will keep SDK default retries at 1 with jitter, and document recommended server-side circuit-breakers for customers using self-hosted SDKs.
- Rollout strategy: blue-green for router changes with canary at 5% traffic, monitor 5xx and retry-amplification metrics for 30 minutes before expanding.
implementation_plan:
1) Router patch: add admission control and X-backpressure header (ENG-4132) — 3 points.
2) Gateway config: tighten circuit-breaker thresholds and add cool-off (ENG-4110) — 2 points.
3) SDK updates: default retries->1 + jitter (merged, release 0.12.2).
4) Health-check agent change for Dedicated pools (config-only rollout) — ensure no restart required.
5) Integration test: add a replay scenario that simulates 500rps + retry storms.
6) Canary rollout plan + rollback runbook.
canary_and_rollout:
- Canary: enable router admission control for 5% of traffic in prod-us-west-2 for 60 minutes.
- Metrics to watch during canary: 5xx rate, retry-amplification ratio, p99 latency, per-route queue length, and customer-facing error count.
- Rollback criteria: sustained 5xx increase > 0.5% over baseline or customer error emails within the canary window.
- Full rollout: 1h -> 5h -> 24h expansion windows after successful canary.
acceptance_criteria:
1) 5xx rate returns to baseline (<0.3%) under simulated retry-storm workload in integration harness.
2) Retry-amplification ratio < 1.2 for all routes under test.
3) No customer-visible increase in tail latency (p99 should not worsen >5%).
4) Health-check flapping reduced and dedicated pool failovers happen within expected SLA.
5) Post-deployment runbook executed and signed off by oncall and SRE.
